content.what_it_is: Fortran module PARAM (L53-L93) centralizes compile-time precision/MPI datatype selection and fixed physical/numerical constants, plus shared scratch variables. DOUBLE_PRECISION selects SP=8 (L58-L59); otherwise SP is obtained with SELECTED_REAL_KIND(6,30) (L63-L64). Under PARALLEL it imports MPI (L54-L55) and maps MPI_SP to the matching MPI datatype in each precision branch (L60-L61, L65-L66). ITERATION conditionally adds mutable initialized iteration controls (L87-L90).
entities: MODULE PARAM declared at L53 and ended at L93
USE MPI module association, conditional on PARALLEL, at L55
SP integer compile-time parameter declared in mutually exclusive precision branches at L59 and L64
MPI_SP integer compile-time parameter declared under PARALLEL in the two precision branches at L61 and L66
pi, R_earth, SMALL, LARGE, grav, zero, RHO_AW, RHO_AIR, RHO_WATER, and DEG2RAD REAL(SP) parameters declared at L71-L80
I, J, K, and RES shared INTEGER variables declared at L83
itmp1, itmp2, itmp3, itmp4, and itmp5 shared INTEGER variables declared at L84
tmp1, tmp2, tmp3, tmp4, and tmp5 shared REAL(SP) variables declared at L85
ITER_NUM initialized INTEGER variable, conditional on ITERATION, declared at L89
ERRORi initialized REAL(SP) variable, conditional on ITERATION, declared at L90

verbatim_spans.text: REAL(SP), PARAMETER:: RHO_AW = 0.0012041_SP  ! relative to water

unresolved: Cross-line consistency defect: DEG2RAD is 0.0175_SP at L80, whereas the same module's pi=3.141592653 at L71 implies pi/180 approximately 0.0174532925; the literal conversion factor is therefore inconsistent with the local pi definition (about 0.27% high). The source does not state whether this coarse approximation is intentional.

Cross-line consistency defect: RHO_AW is documented as relative to water and set to 0.0012041_SP at L77, but the absolute values RHO_AIR=1.15_SP and RHO_WATER=1000.0_SP at L78-L79 imply RHO_AIR/RHO_WATER=0.00115. The module contains two inconsistent air/water density ratios without explaining which consumers should use.
